candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 22:21-35. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. 2 Pet 2:16.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On the Lord's opening of the mouth of Balaam's ass to rebuke the prophet (Num 22:28), Ephrem reads the wonder as the canonical anchor of the doctrine that the Lord may speak truth from the most unworthy vessels: a Gentile diviner is humbled by his own beast, and the prophecy that follows (Num 24:17) issues from the same mouth that needed an ass's instruction. The verse becomes the typological seed of 2 Peter 2:16's denunciation of Balaam — and of the broader patristic principle that the prophetic gift can pass through mouths whose private life condemns them. Tewahedo pastoral theology cites Num 22:28 as the canonical Old-Testament anchor: receive the word for its truth, not for the messenger's worthiness.
